Testing across weight ∈ {0.5,1,2,5,20,50,200,400} (including a rescaled higher-exponent variant), both chunk12 and chunk12v2 data, multiple pilot cells, multi-seed: only 1 of 20 (weight/power/cell) combinations tested produced a shift exceeding its own paired seed-noise floor, and weight=5 caused real non-convergence (down to 1/5 seeds converging in one cell) at a loss-magnitude fraction (~2.7% of math_loss) a naive derivation would not have flagged as risky. Full numbers, all tables: FINDINGS §22.

E3 — dev_k CARRIES NO SIGNAL ABOUT TRUE DOMAIN BALANCE ON THIS CORPUS (negative result, FINDINGS §25). THE FORMULA IS NOT AT FAULT — the input is. An audit of all three implementations found them correct and mutually consistent (in-loop torch / outer-loop numpy / diagnostic_blocks agree to 7.5e-10 on C6/K=4/T1), and gauge-invariant as designed (mean_dev_k moves by exactly 0.00e+00 under ticket 79's transformation). The fault is that the fitted community assignments these functions read do not identify the communities that generated the data, which originates in corpus sparsity, upstream of chunk13v9.py altogether.

A planted-structure test (synthetic data carrying this corpus's exact degree sequence and weight distribution, passed through the real run_inner_solver; 180 fits) finds dev_k flat with respect to the truth it is meant to measure: a world whose communities are exactly balanced by construction reports mean dev_k ≈0.103, a world containing a 70/30 community reports ≈0.096, and a world containing a 90/10 community reports ≈0.101. Detection of a genuinely mono-domain community, against the balanced arm's own 95th percentile, is 6–22% — at or barely above the 5% false-positive rate. On T1, 56–67% of perfectly balanced synthetic worlds report more imbalance than the real T1 data does.

Mechanism: the fitted communities do not correspond to the planted ones. Hungarian-matched recovery accuracy is 0.31 (social) / 0.39 (semantic) at K=4 against a 0.25 chance level, and 0.38 / 0.45 at K=3 against 0.33 — even when 90% of generated ties are within-community. Degree sparsity is the background condition: live-entity total degree has median 2, and 44–45% of live entities have a total degree of exactly 1 (degree 0 cannot occur, since 'live' is defined as having at least one non-zero entry), rising to 50–55% among social entities. Fitted sharpness is 0.81 (social) / 0.82 (semantic) — the model is equally and spuriously confident in both domains, which is also why an earlier post-hoc null (sharpness-based, the user's original hypothesis) found nothing.

Degree alone is not claimed as the mechanism: recovery by degree bucket is non-monotone and reverses between cells, and the recovery metric is argmax-based, a crude instrument against this model's soft partition. The consistent signal is the domain asymmetry, not a degree law.

Direct consequences, not yet acted on in code: (1) evaluate_domain_balance is summed into sociological_penalty unconditionally and therefore shapes Optuna's second Pareto axis today, on a quantity this test says does not track what it names — the in-loop weight being 0.0 does not protect against that; (2) an outer-loop veto on 'obviously broken' communities cannot be built on dev_k (a 90/10 community is caught 6–22% of the time); the parallel candidate reading community mass (max_share) is a different quantity and is untested — a planted test for it is proposed, not run.

claims.claim_text: Bare cross-reference to §16 (same toy-corpus-calibration caveat category).

§1's identity (U[f1]·W)·(W⁻¹·Z·W⁻ᵀ)·(U[f2]·W)ᵀ = U[f1]·Z·U[f2]ᵀ is correct but unconstrained; it says nothing about whether a non-trivial invertible W keeps U·W and transformed Z non-negative (clamp_(min=1e-7), ticket 74); §1's 'Established' status was never checked against whether this freedom is reachable by a real fitted solution.

Near-separability Tier 1 method: from NMF identifiability literature (Donoho & Stodden 2003; Arora et al. 2012; Huang/Sidiropoulos/Swami 2014), if every community has a near-pure entity in some facet that is strong evidence against reachable blending. Checked across all 6 configs × K∈{3,4}, live entities only (build_presence_masks), purity thresholds 0.5/0.7/0.85.

Known confound: evaluate_socio_semantic_reality's Part B (Doxa hoarding, MAX_MONOPOLY=0.85, chunk13v9.py:1160-1211) penalizes U_prob row-max >0.85 for 4 semantic target_facets only when structurally-propagated signal is spread; auth/affil/journ/art untouched by Part B; each purity witness's degree recorded to check against this confound.

Result table: at threshold 0.5, clean facets 56/56 (100%), confounded 46/48 (96%); at 0.7, 53/56 (95%) / 44/48 (92%); at 0.85, 49/56 (88%) / 41/48 (85%). Even at the strict 0.85 bar most (config,K,facet) cells have a near-pure witness for every community; art (most-connected facet) cleanly assigned with witness degree 60-80.

Correction: original text wrongly stated 0.85-bar failures were '7 of ~104 confounded cells; none in clean facets' naming 3 fringe_atom cells. Correct: 7/48 confounded-facet cells AND 7/56 clean-facet cells (14 total); the 'clean' bucket is actually 5 facets (includes parent_he), and 3 of the 7 clean-bucket failures are parent_he (C2/K3 0.522, C2/K4 0.824, C3/K4 0.650) — parent_he is outside Part B's target_facets (ticket 66, 'flagged, not decided'), so these are real unconfounded near-separability failures.
Remaining 4 clean-bucket failures are auth (C2/K4, C6/K4) and journ (C4/K4 non-converged, C6/K3).

fringe_atom is the recurring confounded-bucket failure in 4 cells, not 3: C1/K4, C3/K4, C4/K4, and C5/K4 (previously omitted). Of the 7 confounded-bucket failures, 4 (not 3) are not fully explained by the Part B/low-degree confound: C1/K4/fringe_atom, C3/K4/cousin_he, C3/K4/fringe_atom, C4/K4/fringe_atom (non-converged, flagged per SESSION_PROTOCOL rule 4).

Near-separability is sufficient, not necessary — its presence is strong practical evidence against reachable blending, but absence in some cells doesn't prove blending is reachable there; a decisive answer requires Tier 2's direct feasibility search for a non-trivial orthogonal W.

Tier 2 method: for each fitted (U_final,Z_final) searched for the largest Givens rotation W(θ) mixing exactly two communities, applied to U_final and Z_final for every active facet/relation simultaneously, before any monitored entry goes negative; excludes ticket 79's rescaling freedom; sweeping all K(K-1)/2 pairwise generators is a complete local check of the tangent space. Coarse scan 0.5°-90° then bisection; same 6 configs × K∈{3,4} grid.

Methodological history: first run used absolute tolerance (reject entry below -1e-4) and returned 0.00° margin for all 54 pairs uniformly, flagged as too clean to trust; diagnosed as floor-clamped entries triggering at vanishing angle; fix applied at the time: monitor only entries ≥1% of column/relation max (MEANINGFUL_FRAC=0.01), producing the originally-reported 0.5°-3.4° margin result.

A later audit pass found MEANINGFUL_FRAC flawed: on C6/K4's auth facet the column-relative 1% mask monitored only 18.3% of entries; averaged across the grid 78-84% of U was excluded per cell; excluded entries are disproportionately the near-zero entries in a witness's other communities — exactly what a blending rotation pushes negative first. Concrete case: a witness row had U_prob=0.071 (U_norm=0.00192, a real non-floor value) excluded solely for sitting below 1% of that column's max.

Corrected re-run replaced the column-relative mask with an absolute one calibrated against the model's clamp floor: literal floor-clamped entries cluster at ≈1.5e-7 (35% of entries), a further 44% sit in [1e-6,1e-4); set FLOOR_EXCLUDE=1e-6 and tightened TOL from 1e-4 to 1e-8 accordingly.

Result: 53 of 54 pairs pinned below 0.05°, most exactly 0.000° in at least one direction (max margin anywhere: 0.57°, C2/K4 pair (1,3)). The 0.5°-3.4° figures previously in this document are superseded and should not be used — they measured feasibility of a masked subproblem, not the real system.

Numerical-precision check: only 3/54 pairs pinned at exactly 0.000° in both directions; 33/54 have neither direction at exact zero; 18/54 show real directional asymmetry between +margin and -margin — pattern is structured, consistent with genuine constraint-binding, not a uniform floating-point collapse.

Scope: this is a local (first-order/infinitesimal) feasibility bound around the fitted solution, not proof no distant rotation loops back to a different feasible point. Within that scope, the corrected finding strengthens §18's conclusion: genuine local blending freedom is essentially absent almost everywhere tested, and now agrees with (rather than contradicts) the original pre-MEANINGFUL_FRAC 0.00°-everywhere run.

Motivation for the distant-rotation extension: any rotation, local or distant, that stays feasible has exactly the same reconstruction loss as the original fit (per §1's exact identity) — unlike a different-seed/different-basin disagreement (§1's Run 2 vs Run 4: recon_loss 0.7593 vs 0.7591, opposite anchor-coherence structure), which loss can distinguish. A distant feasible rotation would be invisible to loss-based selection by construction.

A community's domain-skew identity is not reproducible across independently-trained seeds — confirmed with the pipeline's own §S5 alignment, not just a weaker proxy. Distinct from §18 (this is problem 1a, relabeling across independently-trained fits, not 1b, local rotation freedom within one fit) — the two should not be conflated.

Question: does a community's apparent domain character survive across independent re-fits of the same (config,K), or does it reshuffle? Answering requires aligning communities across seeds first — community index is only meaningful within one fit (§14).

First pass: measured with a single-facet (art-only) Hungarian match on column-similarity, the simplest alignment available, not the pipeline's own method. Result: ~45% (19/42) of (config,K,community) triples had a sign-consistent domain-skew reading across 5 seeds (1000/2000/3000/4000/5000), C1-C6 × K∈{3,4}. Never written up formally.

claims.claim_text: The concern (that weak alignment understated stability) was refuted in the opposite direction from how it was raised — stability was slightly lower under the stronger method: art-only 45% (19/42), §S5 Track A (JSD) 38% (16/42), §S5 Track B (weighted cosine) 40% (17/42).

New finding, only visible with two independent tracks: Track A and Track B agree with each other on only 42/48 (88%) of seed pairs — in 12% of pairs the pipeline's own best method disagrees with itself about which community is which. C3/K4 is the extreme case (1/4 pairs agree; one of its 5 seeds did not converge).

Per-config (Track A), same qualitative pattern as informal first pass, not improved by the stronger method: C1 0/7 (0%), C2 6/7 (86%), C3/C4/C5 ~29% each, C6 4/7 (57%). Denser, more anchor-supported topologies (C2, C6) remain more stable than single-anchor C1 — consistent with §4.15's independent finding about C1's anchor weakness.

Practical implication: the hypothesis that a weak alignment method caused apparently low reproducibility is refuted, not confirmed — the weaker method appears to have overstated stability. A community's domain-skew identity is not a robust, reproducible property across independent re-fits, even measured by the pipeline's own best available tool.

Calibration against chance: 'stable' requires all 5 seeds to share the reference seed's sign; under a fair-coin null the probability of the 4 non-reference seeds all matching by chance is (1/2)^4=6.25%. The observed 38-40% is roughly 6× the chance rate — real, detectable consistency, just far short of reliable ('far above chance, far below reliable').

This sharpens the concern about interpreting domain-skew labels as substantive across anything other than one specific reported fit, consistent with the caveat throughout this document that cross-fit/cross-seed comparisons require relabeling correction (§14/§16/§17). Toy-corpus-calibrated — re-derive at 22k-article scale; a denser corpus could change this either way.

Raised in discussion: a 'stable core / variable periphery' story to explain the fringe_atom/C1 weakness pattern. Flagged as a mere association until tested against alternatives (pure facet effect, pure config effect, unstructured noise) — two analyses (Part A re-decomposition, Part B new per-entity test) run to separate them.

Part A: facet and config effects are both real and additive, not competing. fringe_atom is weak in every config including the strongest (C6: -0.159 below that config's own mean; C2: -0.170). C1 is weak across 7 of 9 facets, including ones strong elsewhere (core_child_he: -0.166 below that facet's own mean). A simple additive model (grand mean + facet effect + config effect) explains 78% of the total variance; residual 22% is interaction or noise.

Part B per-entity correlation table (within config×facet cells): Degree vs Track A mean ρ=+0.011 (23/104 sig pos, 14/104 sig neg); Degree vs Track B mean ρ=+0.053 (27/104, 13/104); U_prob purity vs Track A mean ρ=+0.177 (54/104 sig pos, 24/104 sig neg); purity vs Track B mean ρ=+0.073 (39/104, 31/104). Raw connectivity does not predict individual stability (near-zero mean correlation); confidence of assignment shows a real but partial, inconsistent signal.

Caveat: purity and Track A's similarity measure are both derived from the same row-normalized distribution, so part of the purity/Track-A correlation may reflect mathematical kinship rather than fully independent confirmation — the weaker Track B result (close to a coin flip) is probably the more trustworthy read of the effect's real strength.

Revised conclusion: the 'central core, drifting periphery' story is not supported. What drives cross-seed reproducibility is mostly which facet and which config (additive, 78% of variance), not entity centrality. A confidence-based partial effect exists but is inconsistent, not a reliable law; the unexplained residual is consistent with genuine unstructured noise, though not directly provable.

Scope not tested: 'centrality' here meant only raw degree and U_prob row-max ('purity'); no graph-theoretic centrality (eigenvector/PageRank/Katz) was tried, and no hypergraph-specific centrality measure was tried for the hyperedge facets. Not a claim these are the right measures — a future revisit should try at least eigenvector/Katz centrality before concluding the core/periphery story is fully closed.

claims.claim_text: The concern precisely: collapse_pen is the only quantity that is (a) derived from Z_scaled and (b) read by Optuna every trial, feeding sociological_penalty (§4.17/§4.20; ticket 81). Worry: Z_scaled can be reshaped by the optimizer without genuine reconstruction change (the same scale-invariance slack §4.2 already closed once for z_offdiag_loss), showing up as a collapse_pen improvement not corresponding to real de-concentration of entities.

Method: two new diagnostic_blocks.py helpers (BLOCKS_VERSION 1.9.0→1.10.0): collapse_mass_share (not a reimplementation — calls production's own _relation_community_share; self-checked, matches evaluate_dimensional_collapse's collapse_score to 0.00e+00) and membership_share_all_facets (pools live-entity mean U_prob rows across all 9 facets with equal weight, never touches Z_scaled).
Test 2 first pass, C1-C6 × K∈{2,4}, production settings: solution-level Pearson r=0.956, Spearman r=0.944; 2/12 cells showed the exploit pattern (mass_max≤0.60 while mem_max>0.60: C2/K2, C6/K2).

Correction: K=2 was flagged as too low-information to trust (with 2 communities both share vectors are mechanically pinned near 0.5). Re-run on K∈{3,4}: solution-level Pearson r=0.506 (p=0.093, not significant), Spearman r=0.748 (p=0.0051); community-level Pearson r=0.420 (p=0.0056), down from 0.872. The K=2-inclusive correlation was substantially inflated by low degrees of freedom. 0/12 cells showed the exploit pattern at K∈{3,4}.

Test 1: hand-picked lambda_z_offdiag sweep (0.0→2.0, 40× production), C1-C6 × K∈{3,4}, 48 fits. collapse_pen fired in only 1/48 fits (0.0028, C1/K=4 at lz=2.0). Raising lambda_z_offdiag mostly increased mass_max (10/12 cells) — opposite of what a 'cheap collapse_pen improvement' exploit would need. Correlation between mass_max delta and mem_max delta was weak, not significant: Pearson r=0.478 (p=0.116), Spearman r=0.357 (p=0.255). One cell (C3/K=4) showed the exploit shape in its delta but collapse_pen was 0.0 both before and after.

Test 3 (a U_scales-shrinking signature check) was deliberately not run: collapse_pen is built on Z_scaled specifically because §4.2 already closes the U_scales-inflation/Z_pos-shrinkage loophole by construction, and Tests 1-2 show little live pressure for that mechanism to matter in practice. Skipped by agreement, low expected value.

Test 4 intro: a real Optuna study letting NSGAIISampler search lambda_z_offdiag ~ log-uniform[1e-4,1.0] (the real search space, lambda_l1=0 fixed per ticket 78) — testing whether the actual search process finds and exploits the proxy, not just whether it's hackable in principle (citing Skalse, Howe, Krasheninnikov & Krueger NeurIPS 2022; van Laarhoven 2017 — citations from memory, flagged for verification before formal use).

The exploit pattern occurred 4/240 trials, all in C5/K3: at lambda_z_offdiag 0.6351/0.2915/0.7579/0.2137, mass_max was 0.484/0.496/0.480/0.580 while mem_max was 0.630/0.613/0.634/0.604, and collapse_pen read 0.0000 in all four (all converged). All four sit at the high end of lambda_z_offdiag (0.21-0.76), opposite the end where collapse_pen actually fires in this same config.

Stronger than '4/240' alone suggests, checked on a later audit pass: each cell drew 20 trials from only 19 distinct lambda_z_offdiag values (one repeat); the 4 flagged trials in C5/K3 are exactly the 4 highest of those 19 draws — 4 of 4 high-lambda draws show the pattern, not 4 scattered flukes. Convergence in this run: T1 1,126/1,200 and T2 1,130/1,200 trials converged; weakest cells T1/C4/K=4 (45/100) and T2/C5/K=4 (33/100). Run note: study executed in two parts (18 cells initial, 6 cells resumed after wall-clock limit) differing in PYTHONHASHSEED (open ticket 85); cells are independent studies so per-slice pooled statistics are unaffected, split recorded in resume_events.

T1 (Test 4) convergence at K=4: C4/K4 9/20 (45%), C2/K4 14/20 (70%), C3/K4 17/20 (85%), C1/K4/C5/K4/C6/K4 all 20/20. Every T2 K=4 failure hit exactly the 2000-epoch ceiling, and failure lambdas spread across nearly the entire search range, unlike T1's floor-clustering; T2's average epoch counts were much higher (572-1975) — a different mechanism from T1's.

Combined verdict: C4/K4 is the weakest cell on both slices (45%→15% converged, T1→T2), the single most consistent piece of negative evidence against any config in this document. C3/K4 is weak specifically at T2 scale, not T1. These are unrelated to C1's separately-known single-anchor weakness (§4.15) — three different configs, three different mechanisms.

Follow-up question: does Z_scaled's full diagonal/off-diagonal pattern (not just collapse_pen's one scalar) track independent structure? Answer: yes, moderately, and the decline under lambda_z_offdiag pressure is confirmed real, not noise. collapse_pen reads only max_share; this says nothing about whether the raw diagonal/off-diagonal values §1 and this document's community-coupling interpretation depend on can be reshaped by the same training-dynamics-driven slack.

Method: an independent reading data_reading[k1,k2] = U_prob_f1[:,k1]ᵀ @ X_r @ U_prob_f2[:,k2], measuring how much of a relation's real raw edges connect entities plausibly in k1/k2, never touching Z, compared against Z_scaled's own full K×K reading, both normalised to sum to 1 (diagonal and off-diagonal).

A methodological correction happened mid-investigation: the first version read Z_scaled as raw |Z[k1,k2]| shares with no Hungarian permutation correction, flagged as possibly flawed since §14 documents a relation's raw diagonal can be legitimately scrambled. The 'fix' extended _hungarian_relabel_relation to the full K×K matrix (diagnostic_blocks.relation_share_matrix, self-checked bit-for-bit against production's diagonal, 0.00e+00 diff).
Applying the Hungarian-correction 'fix' made every correlation weaker, not stronger: pooled Spearman 0.663→0.599; diagonal 0.660→0.562; off-diagonal 0.422→0.343.

Working through why revealed the fix was based on a wrong diagnosis: Z[k1,k2] is already indexed by U_prob_f1's own column k1 and U_prob_f2's own column k2 by construction — there is no representational ambiguity to correct for against data_share's native indexing. _hungarian_relabel_relation corrects a different problem (community index offset across facets, relevant to collapse_pen's aggregate accounting); applying it here breaks alignment rather than fixing it. Conclusion: the original raw (uncorrected) method was the methodologically appropriate one — reverted to it as primary.

Primary result (raw method, confirmed across two independent runs on the same 48 cached T1 fits): pooled Pearson r=0.733, Spearman r=0.660 (n=4,588) — meaningfully stronger than the max_share-only comparison. Diagonal (n=1,288): Pearson r=0.613, Spearman r=0.656. Off-diagonal (n=3,300): Pearson r=0.630, Spearman r=0.416.

Spearman shows off-diagonal terms tracking the independent reading noticeably worse than diagonal terms — within-community coupling readings from Z_scaled are more trustworthy than between-community coupling readings; an explicit caveat is warranted wherever the article leans on Z's off-diagonal to claim a between-community relationship.
Under increasing lambda_z_offdiag pressure (0.0→2.0), correspondence declines mildly but consistently: Spearman falls 0.693→0.677→0.638→0.595 (Pearson: 0.765→0.737→0.747→0.723) — a decline of 0.098.

Calibration check: re-ran the correlation across 5 independent seeds at fixed production lambda_z_offdiag=0.05, same C1-C6×K∈{3,4} grid (60 fits, 1 non-converged excluded: C3/K4/seed=2000). Seed-to-seed Spearman spread at fixed lambda: 0.035 (range [0.682, 0.717]). The lambda-driven decline (0.098) is 2.8× the seed-to-seed baseline spread — the erosion under lambda_z_offdiag pressure is a real, lambda-driven effect, not ordinary seed variability.

Net effect: Z_scaled's full diagonal/off-diagonal pattern is meaningfully grounded in real structure overall, but off-diagonal values specifically are the weaker link and their correspondence erodes under lambda_z_offdiag pressure by a margin confirmed to exceed noise. Distinct from §18 (which tested static rotational freedom within one fit, found narrow) — related but not the same question. This test used T1 only; not yet replicated on T2.

claims.claim_text: D2's entity-weighted spread inflation, made exact: §13's update measured dev_k's spread growing under entity weighting (mean dev_k ≈0.08 equal-weighted → ≈0.13 entity-weighted), flagged as possibly mechanical. Derived exactly via soc_k=Σ_f w_f·p_f[k] model: idiosyncratic-noise contribution to Var(soc_k) is σ_e²·Σ_f w_f² (Herfindahl concentration index; 1/Σw_f² is Kish's effective sample size), minimized by equal weights.

Table: equal Σw² (n_eff) vs entity Σw² (n_eff) for social/semantic T1/T2, predicted SD ratio √(entity/equal): Social T1 0.250(4.0)→0.588(1.70), ratio 1.53×; Social T2 0.250(4.0)→0.577(1.73), 1.52×; Semantic T1 0.200(5.0)→0.238(4.21), 1.09×; Semantic T2 0.200(5.0)→0.237(4.23), 1.09×. Social collapses from an effective 4 facets to ~1.7 (auth's ~75% share); semantic barely moves (no facet exceeds ~32%).

Checked directly against actual sd(r_k): T1 equal 0.0967, entity 0.1519, observed ratio 1.571×, predicted ratio 1.533×; T2 equal 0.0977, entity 0.1417, observed ratio 1.450×, predicted ratio 1.519×. A parameter-free prediction from facet headcounts alone lands within 2-5% of the observed spread increase.

The mean/median shift toward semantic (mean(r_k) dropping from ≈0.494 to ≈0.465 under entity weighting, both slices, flagged in §13 as unexplained) is the same mechanism, not a second mystery. The hypothesis that auth is less decisively assigned than the small social facets was tested and refuted: auth's median row-max (0.999) is higher than journ's (0.934) or affil's (0.920), not lower.

Σ_k soc_k = 1 is an algebraic invariant for any weighting scheme, so mean_k(soc_k)=1/K identically under equal and entity weighting — confirmed: mean(soc_k)=0.2857(T1)/0.2941(T2) under both weightings, while var(soc_k) roughly doubles (0.0140→0.0336 T1, 2.39×; 0.0158→0.0408 T2, 2.58×) and 14.3%(T1)/5.9%(T2) of communities are pushed under soc_k=0.10 under entity weighting only (vs 0% equal).

r_k = soc_k/(soc_k+sem_k) is concave and increasing in soc_k for fixed sem_k; a variable with the same mean but higher variance passed through a concave function has a lower expected output, so entity weighting's Herfindahl-driven spread mechanically lowers mean(r_k) with no separate cause needed — the earlier 'unexplained, needs its own investigation' framing is withdrawn as the same mechanism as the spread increase.

The spread/mean analysis compares two weighting schemes against each other; it says nothing about how reliable a single fit's r_k reading is in absolute terms — the question needed to set TOL so it exceeds genuine noise rather than firing on communities that are not actually imbalanced, just unluckily seeded.

Method (domain_balance_seed_noise.py): for each (config,K,slice) cell, refit at 5 seeds (MASTER_SEED + 4 offsets), same data/hyperparameters (lambda_l1=0, lambda_z_offdiag=0.05), only RNG differs. Each non-reference seed is realigned onto the reference seed's labeling via s5_dual_track_alignment's Track A (JSD/probability-space Hungarian assignment) — faithful reuse of production's own §S5 stability-analysis alignment code. r_k (entity-weighted, u_prob space) recomputed under each seed's aligned labeling; across-seed SD per community is the noise floor. Smoke-tested: C1 (single-anchor) showed much larger seed-to-seed swings than C6 (dual-anchor) in a 2-seed pilot, confirming the alignment step is doing real work.

Full grid (C1-C6×K∈{3,4}×T1/T2, 5 seeds each; 76 usable community-cells, 2 skipped for reference-seed non-convergence: T2/C3/K4, T2/C4/K4): noise SD(r_k) mean 0.134, median 0.144, p90 0.192, max 0.229. Paired against each community's own dev_k: only 46% exceed own noise SD, 21% exceed 1.5×, 13% exceed 2×. Strongest genuine cases T1/C1/K4 comm1 (dev_k=0.108, noiseSD=0.024, ratio 4.5×) and T2/C2/K4 comm2 (dev_k=0.322, noiseSD=0.141, ratio 2.3×); weakest T1/C3/K3 comm2 (dev_k=0.009, noiseSD=0.140, ratio 0.06).

Single-fit vs multi-fit reliability: averaging several aligned seeds' r_k readings would give a materially more reliable point estimate (the 'stability/consensus across seeds' idea already named in §10), but the in-loop penalty must compute r_k from the model's current parameters at every training epoch — 'average over 5 seeds' is inherently post-hoc/multi-run and cannot be the in-loop training signal. Multi-seed averaging is available for the outer-loop audit after Optuna picks a config, but a further limit: if seeds land in substantively different, comparably-good local optima (§9's non-convexity), more seeds sharpen the estimate of that uncertainty rather than eliminating it.

The 5 grammar relations (M_Atom_Child, M_Child_Parent, M_Fringe_Cousin, M_Cousin_Parent, M_Cousin_Child) are genuinely unweighted (build_grammar_csr, weight≡1). Connects directly to §9's already-documented limitation that ubiquitous semantic elements are structurally disfavoured. Extending weighting to these relations is a concrete, evidence-backed candidate fix.

What S_Art_Auth's log-damping actually does, verified exactly: damped_mass=log2(1+degree); weight(r,c)=count(r,c)*damped_mass/degree. Confirmed to match the real matrix to 4 decimal places (article 17, degree=65, actual_mass=6.0444=predicted log2(66)=6.0444).

Per-tie weight reverses rather than compresses: degree-65 article's per-tie weight is 0.093, degree-6 article's is 0.468 — each tie in the smaller article counts 5× more individually.

The per-tie redistribution — not just total-mass compression — is the actual mechanism serving the stated design goal (avoiding mono-article communities built around one high-author-count article): without it a 65-author mega-collaboration could pull all 65 co-authors strongly toward one community; any extension to grammar relations should preserve this per-tie property deliberately, not just replicate total-mass compression.

claims.claim_text: WHERE THE FAULT LIES. This is a black-box result: it measures what the pipeline reports, not how it computes it. A subsequent line-by-line audit of the implementations found the formula is correct and faithful; all three copies of it agree to 7.5e-10 on a real fit. The failure is therefore not in the arithmetic of evaluate_domain_balance or its in-loop counterpart. It is in the input: the fitted community assignments those functions read do not correspond to the communities that generated the data, so a faithful reading of them carries no information about true balance. claims.claim_text: Stage 1 — the sharpness hypothesis, tested directly and REFUTED. domain_balance_null_baseline.py (no refits; reads the same cached fits as domain_balance_measurement.py). Every live entity keeps its own membership profile, so each domain keeps its own sharpness and headcount, but which community holds an entity's largest value is drawn from one community-size vector shared by both domains. 2,000 draws per fit, 24 fits. Sharpness is near-identical between the domains (0.797 vs 0.814 T1; 0.814 vs 0.794 T2), differs in opposite directions in the two slices, and equalising it changes the expectation by at most 0.002. Across the 24 fits the Spearman correlation between the per-fit sharpness gap and the observed imbalance is -0.06 (p=0.77). Even the most favourable cell (T2/C3/K=3, gap 0.935 vs 0.787) has its expectation raised only from 0.014 to 0.031 against an observed 0.121. The sharpness hypothesis as stated does not explain the observed imbalance.

The observed values sit 5.5x (T1) and 5.8x (T2) above this null, and 61 of 84 communities exceed their own 95th percentile. That is not evidence the imbalance is real: this null assigns entities independently, while real entities are clumped (one many-author article moves all its authors together), so it understates chance variation by construction — stated in the script's own header before the numbers were read. Stage 2 supplies the test that does not have this weakness.
claims.ground_truth_hint: explicit statement of the null baseline's own known weakness, documented in script header

claims.claim_text: Stage 2 — planted structure through the full pipeline: the measure carries no signal. domain_balance_planted_null.py. Synthetic data, real fits (production run_inner_solver, lambda_l1=0, lambda_z_offdiag=0.05, MASTER_SEED, no cache). C1/C3/C6 x K in {3,4} x T1/T2 x 3 replicates; 180 fits, ~25 min. Generative model: every live entity of every facet is assigned a planted community. In the BALANCED arm the same categorical is used for social and semantic facets, so true r_k = 0.5 for every k by construction. In the POWER arms the two differ so that one community has true r_j = 0.70 or 0.90. Ties are rewired preserving each live row's exact degree, drawing column endpoints proportional to their real column degree with a boost for columns sharing the row's planted community. The real matrix's own nonzero values are shuffled onto the new ties, preserving the weight distribution while decoupling it from the planted structure. Generator validated: achieved within-community tie fractions were 0.57/0.75/0.90 against targets 0.60/0.80/0.95. Planted truth confirmed present: true mean dev_k 0.023 (balanced), 0.117 (70/30), 0.236 (90/10).

Headline — reported vs true, pooled over both slices at within-fraction 0.8: exactly balanced truth (true mean dev_k 0.023) reports mean dev_k 0.103, max dev_k 0.158; 70/30 truth (true 0.117) reports mean 0.096, max 0.163; 90/10 truth (true 0.236) reports mean 0.101, max 0.159. The reported value is ~0.10 regardless of the truth. Detection rate, taking the balanced arm's own 95th percentile of max dev_k as threshold: 11%/22% (T1) and 11%/6% (T2) for the 70/30 and 90/10 worlds respectively — at or barely above the 5% false-positive rate. The distributions overlap almost completely: T1 balanced max dev_k spans [0.077, 0.292] median 0.183, T1 90/10 spans [0.049, 0.304] median 0.167 — a lower median for the more imbalanced truth.
claims.ground_truth_hint: diagnostic_results/domain_balance_planted_null.json confirmed present; contains the headline numbers

claims.claim_text: Balanced arm against the real data (same three configs, so like-for-like): real per-fit mean dev_k is 0.095 (T1) and 0.107 (T2); the balanced synthetic world reports 0.106-0.127 (T1) and 0.072-0.088 (T2) depending on structure strength. 56-67% of perfectly balanced T1 worlds report more imbalance than the real T1 data does; for T2 the figure is 17-33%. The observed imbalance lies inside the range exact balance produces.

Mechanism: the communities themselves are not recovered. Accuracy of the fitted argmax community against the planted one (Hungarian-matched on the pooled contingency table), balanced arm: K=3 social 0.38 / semantic 0.45 (chance 0.33); K=4 social 0.31 / semantic 0.39 (chance 0.25). Even at the strongest planted structure (90% of ties within-community) social recovery reaches only 0.37-0.41. When fitted communities do not correspond to true ones, imbalance planted in a true community is smeared across the fitted ones, and dev_k reads how the fit happened to divide the two populations rather than anything about the generating structure.

Degree sparsity is a property of the real data, not of the simulation (the degree sequence is taken from the real matrices): live-entity total degree across all active relations has median 2, mean 5.0, and 44-45% of live entities have a total degree of exactly 1 — verified directly; the minimum over live entities is 1 and degree 0 never occurs, since build_presence_masks defines "live" as having at least one non-zero entry. Among social entities specifically the single-tie share is 50% (T1) / 55% (T2), with median degree 1. A single-tie entity contributes one observation against the K free parameters of its own U row, so most of its placement is fixed by initialisation, the shared Z and the regulariser rather than by evidence about that entity.
claims.ground_truth_hint: build_presence_masks confirmed as a real function per CLAUDE.md §3/§11 (ticket 60); degree statistics in diagnostic_results/domain_balance_planted_null.json

claims.claim_text: Stated as a caveat rather than a mechanism: degree alone does not cleanly predict recovery, and this section does not claim it does. Recovery measured by degree bucket is not monotone and reverses between cells, and the recovery metric itself is argmax-based, which is a crude instrument against this model's soft partition — a multi-community entity is not necessarily a misassigned one. What is consistent across cells is the domain asymmetry above, not a degree law.

The sharpness finding, revisited and sharpened. Fitted sharpness in these synthetic fits is 0.81 (social) and 0.82 (semantic) — near-identical, matching the real fits, while assignment accuracy is near chance. The model is equally and spuriously confident in both domains. That is why Stage 1's post-hoc null found nothing: sharpness is equal, but equally uninformative. This is consistent with, and supplies a mechanism for, two findings already in this document: §19 (a community's domain-skew identity is not reproducible across independently-trained models) and §21 (the seed-noise floor is comparable to or larger than the dev_k signal).
